rationale: Fhourstones-3.1 is a small, compute-bound Connect-4 search benchmark (hot recursive game-tree search with heavy integer/bitboard arithmetic and small hot loops), so the table favors low-cost arithmetic and control-flow obfuscation while penalizing overhead-heavy transforms. SUB is weighted strongly (high SecurityGain, minimal RuntimeCost/CorrectnessRisk) because bitwise/logic substitution is nearly free yet obscures the bitboard operations at the core of the solver. FLA and BCF are useful for hiding the search's control flow but carry high per-iteration overhead in tight recursive loops, so their high RuntimeCost weights keep them selective — applied to colder functions rather than the inner search. IBR adds branch indirection with moderate cost and is kept mid-range to diversify control flow beyond FLA alone. SPLIT is cheap but weak, kept as a low-weight diversifier. ICALL and especially IGV are de-emphasized: Fhourstones has few calls/globals to hide, indirect dispatch costs performance in hot code, and IGV's global-variable indirection carries the highest CorrectnessRisk for pointer- and array-heavy C code, where a miscompile would silently corrupt search results.
